findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Potential XML Injection via String Formatting
 * @description constructing XML using string formatting can lead to XML injection if input is not escaped.
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity warning
 * @id py/xml-construction-formatting
 * @tags security
 *       external/cwe/cwe-116
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking

from DataFlow::Node node, string template
where
    (
        // Check for f-strings or format calls
        exists(DataFlow::Node formatString |
            // f-string (approximated by looking for high number of parts or specific context, but CodeQL handles this via specific nodes)
            // or .format() call
            (
                node.asExpr() instanceof StringLiteral and
                template = node.asExpr().(StringLiteral).getText() and
                (template.regexpMatch(".*<.*>.*") and template.matches("%<%"))
            )
            or
            (
                exists(Call call, Attribute attr |
                    call.getFunc() = attr and
                    attr.getName() = "format" and
                    attr.getObject() = node.asExpr() and
                    template = node.asExpr().(StringLiteral).getText() and
                    template.regexpMatch(".*<.*>.*")
                )
            )
            or
            (
                // % formatting
                 exists(BinaryExpr bin |
                    bin.getOp() instanceof Mod and
                    bin.getLeft() = node.asExpr() and
                    template = node.asExpr().(StringLiteral).getText() and
                    template.regexpMatch(".*<.*>.*")
                 )
            )
        )
    )
select node, "Potential XML construction using string formatting with template: " + template
findings.hypothesis: The library might manually construct XML strings using formatting, potentially leading to XML injection.

findings.hypothesis: User input flowing into manual XML string construction without escaping.
